params.body:
Nightwatch 22 and 23: `stocklist:dailyexport` exited 1 at 05:45, and that is the task that sends the biddings at 07:45. Nobody got their mail that morning, dealer nor trader.

The template walked four photo candidates with `Storage::disk('vehicles')->exists($path)`, and Flysystem demands a string: a `null` is a `TypeError`, not a "no". One vehicle in the first dealer's list had no `trans_thumbnail_path`, and that ended the round. Not a vehicle without photos — that case was handled — but a photo row with one empty derived name.

Reading further turned up that the exception escaped the **loop over recipients**, so everyone after the first bad vehicle also got nothing, and their mails were fine.

**It had been silent for six days.** The last daily mail left on 15 September at 07:47. Eleven biddings arrived since, and none of the 424 dealers and 3 traders with "one mail per day" heard about any of them — they get no creation mail, so this is their only channel. Fixing the crash alone would not have helped: the selection asked for vehicles touched in the last day, and nine of those eleven fell outside that window. They would have stayed silent forever.

So the selection changed question (R B1-2.4): not "is this fresh" but **"has this recipient had it yet"**, read from the row that `export_mailing` already writes per recipient and vehicle. Every bidding leaves once, a vehicle is not re-announced because someone changed a comma, and an interrupted task catches up by itself. Send first, then record: a failed send writes no rows and is retried, which makes silence impossible at the cost of a rare duplicate — the right way round for a digest.

`App\Support\MailPhoto::first` picks the first candidate that is really there, skips an empty name without asking the bucket, and returns `null` so the template falls back to the default image. The round now sends per recipient: one failure is logged and reported, the next recipient still gets their mail. That is the same lesson as the webhooks, and the real one here.

**The mail itself was reworked with Shane, reading it at each step.** The button column per row is gone — the photo and the title are the link, which gives the specs the width they needed; one button at the end, carrying the three-bar mark; a greeting that follows the clock (the 07:45 run says "goedemorgen", a manual afternoon run does not); the count in the heading; the closing date per row, in house amber only when it closes today or tomorrow and quiet grey otherwise; alt text on every photo, because B2B clients block images by default and the mail was a column of empty boxes without it; the mark also added as `stocklist-mark.svg`, drawn from the logo's own geometry rather than cropped.

Two things caught by looking rather than reasoning. A Blade comment and a `@php` block inside the table left blank lines behind, which ends a Markdown mail's raw-HTML block: twelve escaped tags would have arrived at 424 dealers as visible `<td>`. And PHPStan caught `diffInDays` returning a float, so `=== 0` never matched and "sluit vandaag" would never once have appeared. `merchants` has no `name` column either, which would have been a SQL error for every trader; they get their own name or firm.

New rule R B1-2.16. `OneVehicleWithoutAPhotoNameTest` renders the real mailable — the suite fakes the mailer everywhere, which is exactly why a broken template reached production — and pins the escaping, the photo choice and the clock. `BiddingMailsTest` now states the new contract and that an announced bidding does not come back.

**After deploy:** the scheduled run at 07:45 catches up by itself. To send today, `php artisan stocklist:dailyexport` on production; it refuses outside production.

Fixes bevinding een-wagen-zonder-fotonaam-stopte-elke-dagmail.
params.title: One vehicle without a photo name stopped every daily mail
